findings.text: the refusal is asserted only by calling _refuse_altered_shared_parts directly at :738 and :773, never through process_generate_docs_batch, and nothing asserts that persist_generated_docs was not called, so moving the call at worker_generate_docs.py:951 to after the persist would leave both tests green; the done_when requires the refusal be reached on the path the pipeline takes and not only when called directly.

the refusal can never fire for an altered part on the pipeline path: _documentation_with_registry_form appends every stored sentence at :674 through replace_altered_shared_parts, and shared_part_findings at docs_gates.py:1074 only reports SHARED_PART_ALTERED when the stored sentence is absent, so a paraphrase whose overlap falls below 0.75 is kept beside the appended sentence and is neither removed nor refused nor reported.

the refine stage renders through _documentation_with_registry_form and stores normalize_description_text(result_obj.description) with neither description_with_population nor _refuse_altered_shared_parts, so a refinement can drop the settled population clause from a description and store a definition that contradicts the population; this file is outside the node's declared fence, so the repair needs a scope grant.

the operators table pairs line_integrated_electron_density with line_integrated_radiance (:45) and time_derivative_of_electron_density with time_derivative_of_magnetic_field (:57), and neither of those two names appears among the fifteen written names the same file reports at written_names.names, so a reader cannot tell which population each table was measured over; the census has no committed script beside its three sibling censuses either, so it cannot be re-run.

_word_set and _sentence_overlap re-implement the Jaccard ratio that imas_codex/standard_names/review/audits.py:529 _token_overlap already owns, and harmonize.py:107 computes it a third time at a 0.5 threshold while this module uses 0.75, so the census counts a 0.6-overlap restatement as the same form while the gate does not call it altered.

_joined_opening turns a colon-terminated opening into a sentence: 'Its continuum definition is:' has the colon stripped by rstrip(',;:') and is rejoined as 'Its continuum definition is. <note>', breaking the link the colon makes to the text that follows, and the same fragment repair is applied again at :675 by open_without_fragment at docs_gates.py:983, which does treat a colon as a terminator.

assert len(agreed) == 1 holds when every member omits the wording, because written_part_form returns '<omitted>' for each and one omitted form is still one form, so deleting the population installation keeps this test green and it cannot distinguish one wording from no wording.

the gate section publishes the head arm as '94 passed' from gate-head-1311463.log, a log whose header names revision 60654017d -- the base commit, written before the change -- while the 97-pass head log on disk is gate-final-103004.log with no revision or command header at all, and the manifest's test_logs and artifacts cite a gate-final-1311570.log that does not exist.

SharedPartAltered is raised inside the batch's try and caught by the generic except Exception at :989, which calls release_generate_docs_failed_claims and returns the name to pending with no attempt counter, so a name whose model answer keeps contradicting the population is rewritten on every pass at metered cost with no terminal state.

the fragment carries no figure -- no img, svg or figure element -- so the two-arm comparison and the per-part form counts are text only, and the figures write path declared in the fence stayed unused.
